lessons.title: Sharing Opinions

items.example: Det var roligare än jag trodde.
items.exampleMeaning: It was more fun than I thought.

lessons.tip: In Swedish, the past tense is often formed by adding endings to the verb. For example, 'tycka' becomes 'tyckte' in the past.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Gillade du filmen?
dialogue.meaning: Did you like the movie?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ja, jag gillade den.
dialogue.meaning: Yes, I liked it.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Tyckte du att den var intressant?
dialogue.meaning: Did you think it was interesting?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ja, den var mycket intressant.
dialogue.meaning: Yes, it was very interesting.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Vad tyckte du om musiken?
dialogue.meaning: What did you think of the music?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Jag tyckte om musiken, den var rolig.
dialogue.meaning: I liked the music, it was fun.

scenario.partnerRole: You are a friend discussing a movie and music with the learner.
scenario.learnerRole: You are sharing your opinions about what you watched and heard.
scenario.brief: Fråga din vän om deras åsikter om filmen och musiken.
scenario.goal: You should express your likes and dislikes.

lessons.title: Talking About Experiences

items.example: Det var roligt att vara där.
items.exampleMeaning: It was fun to be there.

items.example: Jag har njutit av min semester.

lessons.tip: The present perfect tense in Swedish often uses 'har' + the past participle of the verb. For example, 'vara' becomes 'varit'.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Har du varit i Stockholm?
dialogue.meaning: Have you been to Stockholm?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ja, jag har varit där en gång.
dialogue.meaning: Yes, I have been there once.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Har du sett den filmen?
dialogue.meaning: Have you seen that movie?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ja, jag har sett den, den var fantastisk.
dialogue.meaning: Yes, I have seen it, it was fantastic.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Har du provat den nya restaurangen?
dialogue.meaning: Have you tried the new restaurant?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ja, jag har provat den. Det var roligt.
dialogue.meaning: Yes, I have tried it. It was fun.

scenario.partnerRole: You are a friend asking the learner about their experiences in different places.
scenario.learnerRole: You are sharing your past experiences with your friend.
scenario.brief: Fråga din vän om deras erfarenheter av städer och restauranger.
scenario.goal: You should describe your past experiences.

lessons.title: Expressing Likes and Dislikes
lessons.tip: When expressing dislikes, you can use 'inte' to negate the verb. For example, 'gilla' becomes 'gillar inte'.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Tycker du om spenat?
dialogue.meaning: Do you like spinach?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Nej, jag tycker inte om spenat.
dialogue.meaning: No, I do not like spinach.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Vad tycker du om att vänta?
dialogue.meaning: What do you think about waiting?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Jag avskyr att vänta.
dialogue.meaning: I hate waiting.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Gillar du att resa?
dialogue.meaning: Do you like to travel?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ja, jag älskar att resa!
dialogue.meaning: Yes, I love to travel!

scenario.partnerRole: You are a friend discussing likes and dislikes with the learner.
scenario.brief: Fråga din vän om deras åsikter om mat och aktiviteter.
scenario.goal: You should express what you like and dislike.

lessons.title: Reflecting on Experiences

items.example: Det var en bra upplevelse att resa.
items.exampleMeaning: It was a good experience to travel.

items.example: Jag lärde mig mycket om kulturen.
items.exampleMeaning: I learned a lot about the culture.

items.example: Jag kände mig glad efter resan.
items.exampleMeaning: I felt happy after the trip.

items.example: Det var värt det att åka dit.
items.exampleMeaning: It was worth it to go there.

items.text: jag skulle vilja göra det igen
items.meaning: I would like to do it again
items.example: Jag skulle vilja göra det igen.
items.exampleMeaning: I would like to do it again.

lessons.tip: To express your thoughts about experiences, you can use phrases like 'det var' followed by your opinion. This helps to clearly communicate your feelings.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Hur var din resa?
dialogue.meaning: How was your trip?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Det var en bra upplevelse!
dialogue.meaning: It was a good experience!

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Vad lärde du dig?
dialogue.meaning: What did you learn?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Jag lärde mig mycket om kulturen.
dialogue.meaning: I learned a lot about the culture.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Skulle du vilja åka dit igen?
dialogue.meaning: Would you like to go there again?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ja, jag skulle vilja göra det igen.
dialogue.meaning: Yes, I would like to do it again.

scenario.partnerRole: You are a friend asking the learner about their recent experiences.
scenario.learnerRole: You are sharing your reflections on your trip.
scenario.brief: Fråga din vän om deras erfarenheter och rekommendationer.
scenario.goal: You should reflect on your experiences and share recommendations.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Vad tyckte du om konserten?
dialogue.meaning: What did you think of the concert?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Jag tyckte om den, den var rolig!
dialogue.meaning: I liked it, it was fun!

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Har du sett den nya filmen?
dialogue.meaning: Have you seen the new movie?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ja, jag har sett den. Den var fantastisk!
dialogue.meaning: Yes, I have seen it. It was fantastic!

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Tycker du om att prova nya maträtter?
dialogue.meaning: Do you like to try new dishes?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ja, jag älskar att prova nya maträtter!
dialogue.meaning: Yes, I love to try new dishes!

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Vad tycker du om att vänta?
dialogue.meaning: What do you think about waiting?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Jag avskyr att vänta!
dialogue.meaning: I hate waiting!

scenario.partnerRole: You are a friend discussing various experiences and opinions with the learner.
scenario.learnerRole: You are sharing your thoughts on different topics.
scenario.brief: Fråga din vän om deras åsikter och erfarenheter.
scenario.goal: You should engage in a conversation about your likes and dislikes.
